C.input_or_representation_delta: None: original input and result types, hypotheses, and all-history behavior are unchanged.

D.title: Dirac and deterministic kernels
D.candidate: Compute the existing selected point or action and represent its law by FiniteLaw.pure; interpret it by the original Dirac measure in proofs.
D.input_or_representation_delta: Returning FiniteLaw instead of Measure/Kernel changes the result representation. No support enumeration is needed for a Dirac atom; querying an arbitrary event still requires executable membership.

F.title: Finite rational measure embeddings
F.candidate: Retain the existing finite rational atoms; use FiniteLaw.map/bind/eventMass/expectRat before the analytic embedding.
F.input_or_representation_delta: The finite atoms already exist in this construction. Event queries require a Bool predicate; expectRat requires rational rewards. The original Measure-valued result is retained as analytic denotation.

V.title: Non-atomic volume
V.candidate: For unit-interval volume, compute finite rational interval-union probabilities by the implemented RationalIntervals inclusion-exclusion algorithm; retain the original non-atomic measure as denotation.
V.input_or_representation_delta: The implemented RationalIntervals interface takes a finite rational event descriptor and proves agreement with volume and the existing coordinate-one path law. It computes this event family, not the original arbitrary-set Measure result. FiniteLaw does not represent this non-atomic law exactly.

M.title: General measurable pushforward
M.candidate: Push forward effective source laws through effective maps; for a supplied Measure, a measurable-event query reduces to evaluating the supplied measure on a preimage.
M.input_or_representation_delta: The query only consumes a supplied measure evaluator. A general Measure-valued replacement still needs the trimmed outer measure, including nonmeasurable sets; a Bool-event or effective-law interface changes the contract.

K.title: Kernel composition and realization
K.candidate: In the finite rational case, implement joint draws by FiniteLaw.bind and deterministic projection by FiniteLaw.map, retaining the prefix and dependent action bundle.
K.input_or_representation_delta: General analytic kernels need an effective representation and integration procedure. FiniteLaw inputs are a stronger restriction; supplying the composed kernel itself would assume the original conclusion.

B.title: Terminal and domain branching
B.candidate: Use the concrete constructor/Bool terminal test when available, followed by the same killed or absorbing branch.
B.input_or_representation_delta: General measurable terminal/domain sets need an executable decision. Even with that decision, Dirac measures and kernel composition remain. A decision alone does not make the original result computable.

T.title: Complete trajectory laws
T.candidate: Compute finite prefixes from effective one-step laws. In the bounded terminating finite-law case, FiniteCompletePath.completePaths represents the complete absorbing paths exactly.
T.input_or_representation_delta: The general signature admits non-atomic transitions and no finite termination bound. Effective cylinders are a different representation from Measure on all path events; a supplied complete law is not its construction.

P.title: Finite coordinate and prefix laws
P.candidate: Replace a full-trajectory marginal calculation by finite iteration; with finite rational laws use the retained-history executor and FiniteLaw.map/eventMass.
P.input_or_representation_delta: A finite horizon does not make arbitrary analytic one-step kernels executable. Requires effective transition/action laws and event decisions; the full Measure-valued output still crosses the analytic embedding.

Q.title: Conditional distributions
Q.candidate: At a positive finite observation atom, compute the joint finite law and normalize using FiniteLaw.conditionOnFiber; use FiniteConditionalContinuation for continuation payoffs.
Q.input_or_representation_delta: Requires a finite joint law and decidable observation equality. General standard-Borel disintegration supplies no effective conditional kernel. At null prefixes an arbitrary regular conditional version is not pointwise the constructive continuation law.

I.title: Expected utilities
I.candidate: Use expectRat for finite rational laws, the finite-chain solver for its exact absorbing Markov subcase, or FiniteTruncation.approximate for positive-tolerance terminal expectations.
I.input_or_representation_delta: Finite exact algorithms require their stated finite/rational inputs. Approximation requires effective policies, rational rewards/bounds, positive tolerance, and almost-sure reachability. Boundedness/integrability alone supplies none of these algorithms.

E.title: Zero-guarded eventual utility
E.candidate: On lawful absorbing paths with executable terminal decisions and a reachability proof, search for the first hit and return the original payoff; the existing stoppedUtility handles a supplied bound.
E.input_or_representation_delta: The original function is total on every raw infinite path, including nonabsorbing and malformed paths. First-hit search changes that domain/termination contract; eventual constancy cannot be tested by any fixed prefix. A payoff projection is not real-number evaluation.

W.title: Inherited analytic data
W.candidate: Keep the existing structural wrapper and resolve the listed underlying constructions first; there is no separate numerical algorithm in this wrapper.
W.input_or_representation_delta: Replacing its analytic fields by caller-supplied outputs would shift the construction to the caller. Type/proof references alone do not establish a runtime obstruction; the compiler probe does.
